text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A one-day strike by the two main trade unions on Monday demanding full compensation from the government over price hikes and inflation showed they were prepared to overcome political differences and focus on their common grievances.
- British courts sentenced a British businessman to jail for selling milk powder illegally to Albania four years ago.

- The fifth anti-genocide trial against nine ex-senior communist leaders starts in Tirana on Tuesday. The trial of the last communist president Ramiz Alia and two other former ministers is due to begin at a later date, as yet unknown.
- The main opposition Socialist Party plans to join forces with the other opposition parties, the Social Democrats and the Democratic Alliance, in the upcoming local elections.
- U.S. ambassador Marisa Lino in Tirana met the ruling Democratic Party ahead of the local elections.
- Four Albanians charged with forming an unconstitutional communist party were sentenced with up to two and a half years in jail.
- The government agreed on a 25 million leks subsidy for the railway system.
- The main hard currencies, U.S. dollar, German mark and Greek drachma, have been relatively stable over the past week in Tirana's free market.
- Monday was the first day of the new school year for more than 700,000 Albanian pupils but there is a major shortage of textbooks in secondary schools.
- Joint military exercises between Albania and Greece, code-named Poseidon 96, are currently underway in both countries.
